Sailing Alone Around The World by Joshua Slocum.  
Joshua Slocum was the first man to sail around the world alone in a small boat. He personally rebuilt an 11.2 metre sloop-rigged fishing boat that he named the Spray. On April 24, 1895, he set sail from Boston, Massachusetts. More than three years later, he returned to Newport, Rhode Island, on June 27, 1898 having circumnavigated the world, a distance of 46,000 miles (74,000 km).  
In 1899 he described the voyage in Sailing Alone Around the World now considered a classic of travel literature. It is a wonderful adventure story from the Age of Sail and a book of which Arthur Ransome declared, "boys who do not like this book ought to be drowned at once".

author: OnePodcast
description:
Flashover: "La fase critica di un incendio in un ambiente chiuso, in cui la totalità dei materiali combustibili presenti prende fuoco quasi simultaneamente, senza necessità di contatto diretto con il focolaio iniziale, a causa dell’improvviso innalzamento della temperatura che provoca la decomposizione termica dei materiali e il conseguente rilascio di gas infiammabili."  (dal Vocabolario Treccani)


È la notte di Capodanno del 2026, la località sciistica di Crans-Montana, in Svizzera, è affollata e tanti ragazzi hanno deciso di festeggiare il nuovo anno al Le Constellation. Si tratta di un locale di proprietà di una coppia di imprenditori, Jacques e Jessica Moretti. Le Constellation si riempie di ragazze e ragazzi molto giovani, tra cui numerosi italiani, e all’1.26 va in scena quello che è un rito del locale: una cameriera, portata sulle spalle da un collega, raggiunge un tavolo portando alcune bottiglie. In cima ci sono delle candele pirotecniche che sprigionano scintille. La ragazza allunga un po' il braccio destro e i pannelli fonoassorbenti prendono fuoco. Pochi secondi e quel focolaio, ripreso dai tanti cellulari dei ragazzi, si trasformerà in un incendio devastante. Cosa è successo al Le Constellation? E quali sono state le negligenze, gli errori, le responsabilità e le colpe dei coniugi Moretti e di chi doveva vigilare sulla sicurezza?

title: From Pong to GTA VI
author: baradellopublishing@proton.me
description:
Hello,
This podcast tells the story of how a pastime that began in a physics lab grew into the largest entertainment industry on the planet. We start in 1958 and make our way up to *GTA VI*—released on November 19, 2026, and already a record-breaker.
Each episode lasts five to six minutes. Inside, you’ll find true stories, myths to debunk, anecdotes that usually stay confined to online forums, and a few fun facts that will make you sound great at a dinner party.
You don’t need to know how to play, and you don’t need to own a console. All you need is a bit of curiosity. If, by the end of an episode, you find yourself wanting to pick up a controller, then the podcast has done its job.
Episode Index
1.  The oscilloscope and the milk carton. Tennis for Two, Spacewar, Odyssey, and Pong. The birth of it all.
2.  Coins, ghosts, and a gorilla. The golden age of arcades: Space Invaders, Pac-Man, and Donkey Kong.
3.  The great crash and the plumber who saved everything. Atari’s E.T., the desert landfill, Nintendo, and Super Mario.
4.  Tetris, Sonic, and the U.S. Senate. The Game Boy, the war between Sega and Nintendo, and Mortal Kombat.
5.  The leap into three dimensions. Doom, PlayStation, Super Mario 64, and Lara Croft.
6.  Dundee, Liberty City, and the GTA phenomenon. The origins of Grand Theft Auto, from 1997 to San Andreas.
7.  The world connects. Online gaming, World of Warcraft, the Wii, Minecraft, and Fortnite.
8.  Bigger than cinema. The numbers, the art, the science, and electronic sports (esports).
9.  How to start playing. A practical guide for absolute beginners.
10. GTA VI. The day the world held its breath. The phenomenon of the moment.

title: Health & Longevity with Dr. G
author: Dominic
description:
Welcome to the official Podcast channel of Dr. G.


I'm Dr. Dominic Gaziano, a primary care physician with over 25 years of experience helping patients understand their health, prevent disease, and make informed medical decisions.


After decades of working with patients, I've learned that some of the most serious health problems develop long before you notice any symptoms.

High blood pressure, heart disease, diabetes, and other chronic conditions can quietly affect your health for years.


On this podcast, I break down the medical information you need to know in straightforward, easy-to-understand language.


We'll cover:

  • Heart health and cardiovascular disease prevention
  • High blood pressure and cholesterol
  • Diabetes and blood sugar management
  • Preventive medicine and early detection
  • Healthy aging and longevity
  • Medical tests, treatments, and medications
  • Common health mistakes and what to do instead


My goal is to help you understand what's happening inside your body, recognize potential health risks, and ask better questions when you visit your doctor.


No confusing medical jargon. Just practical health information backed by medical science and decades of clinical experience.


Follow for videos to help you take a more active role in your health.


Disclaimer: This channel is for educational purposes only and does not replace personalized medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment from your healthcare professional.

title: Living with CIDP
author: Speakeasy Studios
description:
Living with CIDP is the podcast that gives a voice to a disease most people have never heard of, and the people learning to live with it anyway.

Hosted by John Rubio, a musician and CIDP patient who's spent years navigating misdiagnoses, remission, relapse, and a healthcare system that doesn't always make it easy to get better, this show pulls back the curtain on what it's really like to live with a rare autoimmune condition.

Each episode brings on patients, caregivers, and voices from inside the medical and insurance systems to talk honestly about diagnosis, treatment, the fight for proper care, and the mindset it takes to keep going when the body won't cooperate. This isn't a clinical show, and it's not about sympathy. It's about the real, unfiltered experience of living with a chronic illness and refusing to be defined by it.

Ready to hear the stories no one else is telling? Welcome to Living with CIDP.

title: Foz
author: Bernadette Wesley
description:
Foz means "where the river meets the sea" in Portuguese. Hosted by Bernadette Wesley, this podcast lives in that meeting place, questioning the myth of separation and exploring what becomes possible when we live from interconnection. It's for people who sense the old ways of seeing no longer fit. What does it mean to be both the river and the sea?

Season 1: Organizations That Discern
In this experimental, dialogue-driven series, Bernadette and Ted Rau ask: What if the next stage of organizational development isn't managing complexity better, but learning to consciously participate in a living, creative intelligence that is continuously generating reality? And what practices, structures, and inner capacities would organizations need to cultivate to do that?

title: Cripping Culture Oral Histories
author: Disability Arts Online
description:
Cripping Culture Oral Histories explores the history of the Disability Arts movement through the memories of the disabled artists and activists who shaped it. The series shares achievements, brings previously hidden stories to light and offers new perspectives on key moments in the movement’s history and its role in advancing disability rights from the late 1970s onwards.

Cripping, like queering, uses a reclaimed word to apply a disability lens to culture.

This podcast is part of Cripping Culture: A Journey into Disability Arts Heritage. We are grateful to The National Lottery Heritage Fund and National Lottery players for supporting this project.

title: UnSupervised
author: Andrew Schofield
description:
UnSupervised


Three counsellors. Three perspectives. No supervisor in sight.


Welcome to UnSupervised, the podcast where three counsellors step out of the therapy room and into the conversation.


Join Andy, Donna and Deon as we explore the messy, funny, difficult and sometimes downright ridiculous business of being human. From relationships, anxiety and grief to parenting, work, identity, ageing and everything that happens in between, nothing is necessarily off the table.


We bring three different personalities, experiences and perspectives to the conversation. Sometimes we agree, sometimes we definitely don't, and quite often we end up somewhere none of us expected.


There'll be plenty of therapeutic insight, but this isn't therapy and we're not here to tell you how to live your life. We're three counsellors having the kinds of honest conversations that usually happen when nobody else is listening.


Expect real experiences, different perspectives, dark humour, occasional oversharing and more than a few tangents.
